annotations.shape: hand-written single text/plain message whose Subject is a three-level nested encoded word (each level's base64 payload is another encoded word)
annotations.phase_1_facts: headers.decoded: RFC 2047 decoding is NOT recursive, so one pass over the Subject word yields the level-2 encoded word verbatim as the decoded text
annotations.work_budget: the property a later test asserts is non-superlinear work per input byte (operation counts or a length-scaled ratio, never absolute seconds, single threaded): a recursive decoder would expand the nest, this decode is one pass
annotations.phase_0_facts: only container.sha256, container.size_bytes and part.gaps are typed at phase 0: the skeleton walker applies NO structural cap, so its part.tree/part.regions/decode.chain output for this fixture is the uncapped walk and is not what the intended behaviour (a cap hit) is; typing them would assert the walker's uncapped reading as the expected one. part.gaps is typed because a sidecar must state a gap expectation and the walker records no gap on these bytes (the same under either reading)
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes (offsets and lengths) and typed by a model from the RFC and format rules and the design, never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: a field's raw_span covers its line including the line ending; value_span starts immediately after the colon and keeps the leading space; a part's headers_span includes its closing empty line; the CRLF in front of a boundary line belongs to the delimiter region (RFC 2046), so the regions tile the message exactly
annotations.document_axes: document.axes: the four not-built document axes unknown(not_built_in_phase1) (decision 6)
